methodology.cpu: Aggregate attributable package process utime+stime deltas, actual system CLK_TCK, device uptime; 100% means one logical core. Incomplete/recycled PID intervals are excluded, not counted as idle.
methodology.memory: Per-process dumpsys meminfo PSS summed in MiB; samples approximately every 60 seconds, not instantaneous peak.
methodology.sampling: CPU approximately every 30 seconds, HTTP fixture observations every 500ms; recovery bookkeeping, ADB and PSS sampling overhead included. Not a physical battery, real ChatGPT, or unattended no-probe benchmark.
methodology.platforms: Fresh x86_64 Google APIs emulators with 4096MiB configured RAM. App sources unchanged from prior accepted PoC; no production key or login directory used.

findings: All accepted stages lasted at least 600 real host seconds and retained four original documents, drafts, reading positions and host PIDs without new document requests or automatic submission.

Android15 completed one sequential 30-minute background/screen-off/Doze round plus the original 17 recovery checks. Android9 used a 20-minute Home/screen-off round and a separate 10-minute Doze round plus the original 17 recovery checks; not a single continuous 30-minute result.
The Android9 image lacked getconf; the CI-only shell probe measured actual sysconf values 100Hz and 2 logical CPUs. It was not packaged into the app.

The Android9 image had deep idle disabled by default; the scoped CI test enabled it, waited for screen=false/charging=false, and observed IDLE at all 21 Doze samples. No app whitelist exemption was added.
Android15 Doze observations became stale for approximately 600 seconds while all original documents returned afterwards; this is not proof of continuous JavaScript execution.
PSS increased within parts of the fixed synthetic workload. That does not establish a memory leak; heap/native allocation and pending-network/snapshot bookkeeping analysis remain necessary.

No actual resource optimization or production kernel migration was performed. Emulator results include fixture and sampling overhead and do not predict current System WebView client, real ChatGPT, arm64, OEM scheduling or physical battery usage.
limits: No arm64 physical device or real ChatGPT/login/passkey acceptance.
No aggressive OS memory-pressure or multi-hour/overnight survival guarantee.
Sampled PSS peaks and30-second CPU windows are not instantaneous peaks.
No main/public release/website/local App/login/signing-data changes in this batch.
